label: Acts 27:1
text: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

label: Acts 27:2
text: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea; Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

label: Acts 27:3
text: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

label: Acts 27:4
text: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

label: Acts 27:5
text: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

label: Acts 27:6
text: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.

label: Acts 27:7
text: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

label: Acts 27:8
text: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

label: Acts 27:9
text: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them,

label: Acts 27:10
text: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”

label: Acts 27:11
text: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

label: Acts 27:12
text: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking northeast and southeast.

label: Acts 27:13
text: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.

label: Acts 27:14
text: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

label: Acts 27:15
text: When the ship was caught, and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven along.

label: Acts 27:16
text: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

label: Acts 27:17
text: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.

label: Acts 27:18
text: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

label: Acts 27:19
text: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.

label: Acts 27:20
text: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.

label: Acts 27:21
text: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them, and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.

label: Acts 27:22
text: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

label: Acts 27:23
text: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,

label: Acts 27:24
text: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’

label: Acts 27:25
text: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.

label: Acts 27:26
text: But we must run aground on a certain island.”

label: Acts 27:27
text: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

label: Acts 27:28
text: They took soundings, and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

label: Acts 27:29
text: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.

label: Acts 27:30
text: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,

label: Acts 27:31
text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”

label: Acts 27:32
text: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let it fall off.

label: Acts 27:33
text: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

label: Acts 27:34
text: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”

label: Acts 27:35
text: When he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and he broke it, and began to eat.

label: Acts 27:36
text: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.

label: Acts 27:37
text: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

label: Acts 27:38
text: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

label: Acts 27:39
text: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.

label: Acts 27:40
text: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

label: Acts 27:41
text: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

label: Acts 27:42
text: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.

label: Acts 27:43
text: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;

label: Acts 27:44
text: and the rest should follow, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.

label: Paul and other prisoners were handed to Julius to sail for Italy
statement: When it was determined that Paul and certain other prisoners should sail for Italy, they were delivered to a centurion named Julius of the Augustan cohort.

label: Julius was a centurion of the Augustan cohort (speira Sebastē)
statement: The centurion guarding Paul belonged to the Augustan cohort (Greek speira Sebastē, Latin cohors Augusta), an auxiliary unit reported as attested by inscriptions in Syria during most of the first century.

label: Aristarchus of Thessalonica accompanied Paul on the voyage to Rome
statement: Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, sailed with Paul on the voyage toward Italy.

label: They embarked on a ship of Adramyttium bound for Asian ports
statement: The party embarked in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia.

label: At Sidon Julius let Paul receive care from his friends
statement: The next day they touched at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul kindly, giving him permission to go to his friends and receive care.

label: They sailed under the lee of Cyprus against contrary winds
statement: Putting to sea from Sidon, they sailed under the lee of Cyprus because the winds were contrary.

label: They sailed across off Cilicia and Pamphylia and came to Myra of Lycia
statement: After sailing across the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia, they came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

label: At Myra the centurion transferred the prisoners to an Alexandrian ship bound for Italy
statement: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy and put them on board.

label: Alexandrian grain ships regularly sailed from Alexandria to Italy
statement: Alexandria's grain fleet routinely shipped wheat from Egypt to Italy (Rome) - a trade that required port infrastructure en route such as the granary at Myra's port Andriake.

label: They sailed slowly many days and came with difficulty off Cnidus
statement: They sailed slowly for many days and with difficulty came off Cnidus, the wind not allowing them to hold their course.

label: They passed Cape Salmone at the eastern end of Crete
statement: Sailing below Crete off Salmone, they rounded the island's eastern cape.

label: They put in to Fair Havens near the city of Lasea
statement: Coasting along Crete with difficulty, they came to a place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea.

label: The Fast (the Day of Atonement) had already gone by
statement: Much time was spent and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had already gone by - the Fast is commonly understood as the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur), placing the voyage in late September-October.

label: Autumn sailing was dangerous and the sea closed in winter (mare clausum)
statement: Mediterranean navigation was considered dangerous after mid-September and entirely shut from 11 November to 15 March, a fixed custom of the ancient shipping calendar.

label: The centurion heeded the pilot and shipowner more than Paul
statement: The centurion gave more heed to the master and the owner of the ship than to Paul's warning about the voyage.

label: Phoenix on Crete's south coast was a harbor suitable for wintering
statement: The harbor of Phoenix, looking toward northwest and southwest, was judged suitable to winter in; its identification with modern Loutro is disputed (another Phoenix near Foinikas is named by Strabo).

label: A tempestuous wind called Euraquilo beat down from Crete
statement: A tempestuous wind, called Euraquilo (the northeaster; KJV Euroclydon), beat down from the island - the kind of violent northeasterly Mediterranean wind now called the gregale.

label: They ran under the shelter of an island called Cauda (Clauda)
statement: Running under the lee of a small island called Cauda (Clauda), they secured the ship's boat with difficulty - Cauda is identified with modern Gavdos south of Crete.

label: The crew undergirded (hypozōsantes) the ship with cables
statement: The sailors used helps to undergird the ship - passing cables (hypozomata) around the hull to brace it against the storm, a known ancient nautical practice.

label: Fearing the Syrtis shallows, they lowered the gear and were driven
statement: Fearing lest they fall on the Syrtis (the Greater Syrtis shallows off North Africa), they lowered the sea gear and so were driven.

label: An angel of God assured Paul that all aboard would be saved
statement: An angel of the God to whom Paul belonged stood by him in the night, saying he must stand before Caesar and that God had granted him all who sailed with him.

label: On the fourteenth night they were driven in the sea of Adria
statement: On the fourteenth night the ship was driven about in the sea of Adria - in ancient usage the open sea between Crete, Sicily, Italy and North Africa, not the modern Adriatic.

label: They sounded and found twenty fathoms, then fifteen fathoms
statement: They sounded and found it twenty fathoms; a little further they sounded again and found it fifteen fathoms.

label: They dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for day
statement: Fearing they would fall on rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern and wished for the day.

label: All aboard the ship numbered 276 souls
statement: There were in all two hundred seventy-six souls aboard the ship when they ate and lightened it.

label: Ships on this route carried crews and passengers numbering in the hundreds
statement: Grain ships sailing between Egypt and Italy in the mid-first century could carry several hundred people aboard, crew and passengers together.

label: The ship carried wheat as cargo, thrown overboard to lighten her
statement: When they had eaten, they lightened the ship by throwing the wheat into the sea - confirming the vessel was a grain ship.

label: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent escapes
statement: The soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out and escape - the guarding soldiers answered with their lives for prisoners who escaped.

label: All 276 came safe to land
statement: The rest, some on planks and some on other things from the ship, all came safe to land.
